source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: Accepted nsMsgHdr::GetStoreToken first reads the string property. If it is empty, it reads the legacy msgOffset column with the maximum uint64_t value as the unset sentinel, converts a real value to decimal and persists it through SetStoreToken. Zero is a valid first-message token. The current test inserts msgOffset through setUint32Property to exercise compatibility after messageOffset was removed. The old column remains; the getter/setter do not erase it. Clearing a string on an ancient header can therefore expose the fallback again, so empty-string deletion must not be taught as unconditional permanent removal.
title: Migrate ancient msgOffset values lazily and preserve zero
